_description: Keyed cover-letter variants. Each key is a profile-chosen identifier (e.g. company_role_focus). Two shapes are supported by RFC 036's cl_base_matcher: 'template-variants' (a single `defaults` object — see e.g. lilia) and 'library' (top-level keys map to entries with `paragraphs: [p1, p2, p3, p4]` — see e.g. jared). Optional per-entry metadata fields — `company`, `archetype`, `role_keywords` — are read by the engine matcher to pick the right base; absent fields fall back to key tokenization (e.g. key `affirm_capital` → company `affirm`, keywords `[affirm, capital]`).

example_company_fintech_pm.openingParagraph: Your mission to make credit accessible lines up with work I have led shipping risk-scoring products for similar audiences.
example_company_fintech_pm.bodyParagraph: At Example Corp I drove a roadmap that grew ARR 7x in 18 months while cutting fraud losses by 34%. The wins came from a disciplined loop: weekly cohort reads, tight scope on experiments, and a bias toward shipping the smallest thing that would teach us something.
example_company_fintech_pm.closingParagraph: I would love to talk about where your product is heading next quarter and where I can help.

_library_shape_example._doc: Reference example of the RFC 036 'library' shape. The keys below show the contract the matcher reads. Leading-underscore keys are ignored by the matcher.

paragraphs: P1 hook — company-specific, regenerated per letter.
P2 core proof — locked across letters of the same archetype.
